configurations.// next-dev-handoff: Handoff 22a-27a review server. Own dist dir: a dev server killed mid-compile leaves the previous one locked on Windows, and Next then hangs at Starting forever rather than reporting the lock, so it must not share one with a concurrent session. Runs the local node rather than the npm scripts npx -y node@20, which sat for five minutes without producing a dist dir or a log line.
configurations.name: next-dev-handoff

configurations.// next-dev-visuals-b2: Handoff batch 28a-34a review server. Own dist dir: a dev server killed mid-compile leaves the previous one locked on Windows and Next then hangs at Starting forever, so it must not share a dist dir with a concurrent session.

configurations.// next-dev-playwright: Playwright e2e server on the port playwright.config.ts expects (3101), aimed at the .env.test database by file NAME so no connection string lives in this file. Its OWN dist dir: the default `.next-playwright-<port>` had 22 files COMMITTED to git despite .gitignore listing `.next-playwright-*/` (ignore rules do not apply to already-tracked files), so git and Next wrote the same paths and the server died mid-run with `UNKNOWN: unknown error, open react-loadable-manifest.json` and 500'd every route. scripts/playwright-dev-server.cjs refuses to start against production and cleans its own dist dir; Playwright reuses this server rather than spawning a second. ADMIN_PASSWORD mirrors the throwaway value CI sets for the @admin specs.
configurations.name: next-dev-playwright

configurations.// next-dev-gtm: GTM/dataLayer verification server. Own dist dir per the convention above — a dev server killed mid-compile leaves the previous one locked on Windows. NEXT_PUBLIC_GTM_ID is deliberately UNSET: the point of the check is that lib/analytics/dataLayer.ts queues events with no container present, which is also the real production state until the container is published.
configurations.name: next-dev-gtm

configurations.// next-dev-mobile-qa: Mobile-viewport QA session. Own dist dir per the convention above. DEV_AUTH_BYPASS_* are not secrets — the bypass is gated on NODE_ENV !== production in lib/auth.ts, and the email is set to an EXISTING account so ensureDevAuthUser FINDS rather than CREATES a row. Reads whatever DATABASE_URL .env.local holds; this config adds no connection string of its own.
configurations.name: next-dev-mobile-qa

env.// bypass-identity: ensureDevAuthUser matches on id OR email OR username, and .env.local sets DEV_AUTH_BYPASS_USERNAME=local_dev_user — a username the allfantasysportsapp account now actually carries. Leaving those set lets the OR resolve to THAT row instead of the email one, i.e. signing in as the wrong account. These two are deliberately unmatchable so the email clause is the only one that can hit.

configurations.// next-dev-rail: League-rail review server (the expanded rail on any /core screen). Own dist dir per the convention above. Signs in as the account whose 94 claimed teams and 7 unpaired elimination leagues are the only rows that exercise this surface — by USER_ID, because ensureDevAuthUser matches on id OR email OR username and the other two are deliberately unmatchable so the id clause is the only one that can hit. Reads whatever DATABASE_URL .env.local holds; this config adds no connection string of its own. ⚠ Review a NON-HOME /core screen: the home fires recordDashboardActivation, which is a production write.
configurations.name: next-dev-rail
